assessments.rationale: The supplied public OpenReview comment, signed by the paper's Authors group, explicitly identifies zhouxian/FluidLab as the transferred repository. This supports the official repository relationship, not certification of the pinned commit as the published experiment revision.

The investigation appropriately leaves the published-result match unverified. File hashes identify source snapshots, not exact experimental inputs or results. The reported artifact search is explicitly limited to inspected sources; empty results and absent tags/releases do not establish that no external checkpoints exist.

Treating physical length, time, mass and material-unit mappings as unestablished is justified by the supplied evidence. Numeric geometry, gravity and timestep values do not establish SI units. The sim-to-real excerpt supplies no calibration and does not include Pouring among the four demonstrated tasks. No physical scales can be inferred or invented from it.

The supplied launcher passes renderer_type to gym.make, the registration points Pouring-v0 to PouringEnv, and its constructor accepts neither renderer_type nor arbitrary keyword arguments. This establishes a static interface mismatch, not an observed runtime failure or proof that execution would reach that point before encountering other errors.

The proposed patch narrowly addresses that mismatch by accepting renderer_type, storing it before environment construction, and forwarding it as the type argument accepted by TaichiEnv.setup_renderer. Its GGUI default preserves the existing default selection. Reported application and parsing checks do not establish backend compatibility, successful initialization or simulation correctness; runtime testing remains explicitly absent.

The not-ready conclusion is supported by the unresolved launcher mismatch and untested dependency, compute and rendering compatibility. Missing NVIDIA indicators do not rule out all Taichi backends. Missing SI calibration and published-result artifacts constrain physical interpretation and publication matching, respectively; they are not prerequisites for native-unit execution. Even after the patch, native readiness requires a tested compatible runtime. This assessment makes no execution or scientific-validation claim.

scope: Advisory evidence review only, not runtime or scientific validation.
